node_definition.done_when: Read section 11 of plan-writes-are-not-fenced first, including the measured failure it quotes. First reproduce at your base: call _edit_plan in reckon/mcp.py with a stale expected_version for a section append and for a state set, and show that it raises VersionConflict rather than returning the structured refusal. Then every op path of _edit_plan returns, on a stale expected_version, the same structured refusal the followup and comment paths already return: ok false, error version_conflict, expected_version, current_version, and a message naming both. No path raises it. tests/test_every_edit_path_refuses_one_shape.py drives followup append, section append, state set and comment append with a stale version in a temporary checkout, and asserts the identical refusal shape for each. The section-append and state-set cases fail at your base. tests/test_landing_write_races_every_writer.py must then pass 20 consecutive runs at -n 8 while a concurrent load runs beside it. For the load, start a second pytest -n 8 over tests/test_crew_promotion.py at the same time. Log each run's result to a file under the run directory and keep its last line. Existing tests reaching _edit_plan keep passing; grep tests/ for _edit_plan and edit_plan to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/plan-writes-are-not-fenced/every-edit-path-refuses-one-shape.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
